title: Invariant Exclusion for Boomslang
summary: An affine-layer argument gives a 0.99-probability exclusion at 24 rounds, while small-round guarantees and coverage of generalized or closed-loop invariants remain open.

formal_statement.body: For Boomslang with uniformly chosen random round constants, an existing affine-layer argument shows with probability at least $0.99$ that $24$ rounds suffice to rule out the joint invariants covered by that argument. Determine what invariant-exclusion guarantees can be proved when only a small number of rounds is considered, and extend the analysis to generalized and closed-loop invariants.

scope.domain: Structural cryptanalysis of invariants in the Boomslang symmetric cipher.
assumptions: Round constants are chosen uniformly at random.
parameters: Round count, distinguishing the established 24-round result from the unresolved small-round case
Invariant type, distinguishing the covered joint invariants from generalized and closed-loop invariants
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove invariant-exclusion guarantees for a small number of rounds and extend the analysis to generalized and closed-loop invariants.

citations.label: Constructing and Deconstructing Intentional Weaknesses in Symmetric Ciphers

progress.summary: The source presents a high-probability 24-round exclusion argument for the covered joint invariants and explicitly identifies its lack of coverage for small round counts and generalized or closed-loop invariants.
citation_labels: Christof Beierle et al., Constructing and Deconstructing Intentional Weaknesses in Symmetric Ciphers
